chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Yunus ibn Ya' ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a woman who dies before the man, or a man before the woman, he said: 'Whatever is from the personal effects of women is for the woman, and whatever is from the personal effects of men and women is shared between them, and whoever takes possession of any part of it, it is for him.'
ai.seo_question: How is personal property divided between husband and wife if one spouse dies before the other?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between personal effects and joint property in marital inheritance, establishing possession as the key determinant for ownership. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that items designated for one spouse remain exclusive to them, while shared goods are subject to division, thereby preventing disputes over household assets. This ruling complements the broader inheritance framework by addressing movable property distinct from the fixed shares of the estate.
